whatItIs.text: A British-market spice blend adapted from Indian garam masala — turmeric, coriander, cumin, chilli and friends in a ready-made mix; no Indian household calls this 'curry powder'.

historyNote.text: It was first sold by Indian merchants to British traders in the Company-rule era; the first commercial product was advertised by Sorlie's Perfumery Warehouse on Piccadilly in 1784, and the word 'curry' itself comes from Tamil kaṟi, sauce or relish for rice.

howToChoose.text: Blends vary wildly — smell for brightness, not dust; buy small tins from high-turnover shelves and add it early in cooking so the raw flouriness cooks off.

storage.text: Keep in an airtight jar away from heat and light.

useItUp.text: Dust it over roasted vegetables, whisk into mayonnaise, or shake it into curry; fading powder still shines with fresh ginger and garlic alongside.

substitutions.note: warmer, less sharp; closer to the Indian original
